description: We are a student team interested in space science, planetary exploration, technology and innovation. Our interests include Planet X and Sphere X, and we aim to explore creative, technology-driven solutions to real-world challenges. We welcome members passionate about coding, research, data analysis, scientific problem-solving, design and presentation. We value teamwork, curiosity and collaboration, and are eager to turn innovative ideas into impactful projects.
summary: Project Astrosearch answers the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge with two public web apps that help anyone see how the infrared sky changes over time. NASA's SPHEREx maps the whole sky in 102 infrared colours every six months, but its archive is hard for newcomers to use. COSMOS lets users search a sky position, discover real SPHEREx observation dates from NASA/IPAC IRSA, load real image cutouts for two periods and compare them with a blink comparator, split-screen wipe and date timeline. Sky Blink & Spectral Explorer is a clearly labelled simulation that teaches people to spot objects that shift position between epochs, the way comets, asteroids and brown dwarfs do, and to read a 102-band infrared spectrum. Together they make SPHEREx data easier for students, teachers and citizen scientists to explore.
details:
WHAT IT DOES
Project Astrosearch answers the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge with two linked web apps that let anyone see how the infrared sky changes over time.
- COSMOS (https://cosmos-ahq.pages.dev) searches the official SPHEREx archive, lists real observation dates for a sky position, loads real image cutouts for two periods and compares them with a blink comparator, split-screen wipe and date timeline.
- Sky Blink & Spectral Explorer (https://nasa-citizen-science.netlify.app) is a labelled practice simulator with four epoch modes (blink, wipe, RGB motion map, 4-epoch timeline), a 102-band spectrum explorer (0.75-5.0 micrometres) and a citizen discovery log.

HOW IT WORKS
Users enter RA/Dec or pick a named object, choose a SPHEREx data release, discover the available dates, then compare two periods. COSMOS lists only dates returned by the archive and links each record to the original SPHEREx FITS product. Sky Blink uses simulated data so beginners can practise spotting moving sources and reading spectra first.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT
SPHEREx has imaged more than a billion objects, far too many for one person to sift. Our tools let students, teachers and citizen scientists see change over time in the browser, without special software or knowledge of FITS files.

CREATIVITY
We brought the blink comparator, the technique that revealed Pluto in 1930, to the browser and added a wipe, a timeline, an RGB motion map and a discovery log that turns practice into a game.

HONEST LIMITS
COSMOS images are for visual comparison only. It does not automatically detect asteroids, comets or Planet X. Sky Blink is an educational simulation, not live mission data. Both are independent student projects, not affiliated with NASA.

TOOLS
Browser-based web apps hosted on Cloudflare Pages and Netlify. Data comes from NASA/IPAC IRSA.

Gemi ai was used to create the video,netlify was used to to build, deploy, and host the website
